public_rationale: Ai2 documents that its fully open tooling enables controlled changes to data mixtures and training objectives. That supports the mechanism behind Marcus's comparison. It does not, alone, establish how much less customization, improvement and investigation the open-weight category permits. The retrieved records do not supply a sufficiently complete comparison for the post-date state, so the broad comparative claim remains unresolved.
limitations: The cited comparator predates the target period and is context only.
More available training materials do not by themselves establish larger achievable performance gains.
No conclusion here treats fine-tuning or internal inspection as impossible.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Open-weight models can be run and post-trained but cannot be customized, improved or investigated nearly as much as open-source models.

statement.excerpt: That means you can run them (or “posttrain” them), but, crucially, users can’t customize or improve them to remotely the same degree (more about that in a second), and outsiders can’t investigate them to nearly the same degree.
statement.document_title: Open-source is NOT the same as open-weight

from_speaker: can't customize or improve them to remotely the same degree
can't investigate them to nearly the same degree
our_interpretation: Assess capabilities available as of August 10, 2026.
The comparison with open-source models is a comparator, not a forecast antecedent.
Read the claim primarily through the examples in context: changing original training inputs, repeating original training stages and investigating how training choices affect behavior.
Do not interpret it as saying that released weights cannot be changed, fine-tuned or examined.
Remotely the same degree means a substantial practical gap across these activities, not a specified difference in benchmark scores.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable release records show that weight-only users can run and post-train models but lack materials necessary for a substantial range of original-training interventions and audits that fully open releases enable.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Weight-only releases provide substantially equivalent access to those interventions and audits, or documented comparisons show no substantial practical gap.
